content: Weirdly, I can't find limit and derivative (not of polynomial or power series) in Mathllib.
If you want to search using natural language, try https://deepwiki.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/ or https://leansearch.net/

Can we teach the doc to show HasDerivAt when searching for derivative? (similar for other common abbreviation in mathlib)
Though deepwiki does largely cover this, so probably no need to duplicate the effort, but a lot of these amazing exploration tools aren't obvious to find for new comers

Weiyi Wang said:

a lot of these amazing exploration tools aren't obvious to find for new comers

(I think the better solution is to integrate an LLM into the docs, and have a toggle in the searchbox between fuzzy-search and semantic LLM search)
Or we should make "how to search for results" part of the standard Lean introduction. (It is part of any course I would teach.)
The search box in the docs used to also search docstrings. Bringing this feature back would probably solve the issue at hand
That would indeed be a nice feature to have!
There's also here and here (undergrad) for lists of mathematical topics in mathlib (though as always I'm aware these aren't updated regularly)

Michael Rothgang said:

Or we should make "how to search for results" part of the standard Lean introduction. (It is part of any course I would teach.)

I did exactly this in a class I taught on Lean a few weeks ago! I thought the best way to learn is by doing many examples, so I asked the students to each come up with a theorem they learnt in some other class, then demonstrated in class how I would search for and state these theorems in mathlib, using the various tools we have (docs, LLM search as mentioned above). How to replicate this online / on a larger scale, well this is basically the "ask on zulip" experience :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:
